Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the final run chase as the umpires make their way out to the middle. The West Indies players jog out onto the field and take their respective fielding positions. Innocent Kaia and Tanunurwa Makoni will open the innings for Zimbabwe and it is to be seen if they look to chase down this mammoth total. Kemar Roach has the new ball and will begin proceedings. Let's play...
... FOURTH INNINGS ...

Zimbabwe were looking for wickets early and Brad Evans dismissed the double-centurion from the first inning early. Wellington Masakadza had an extended spell of bowling and sent the other opener back to the shed. He returned to dismiss both the half-centurions and ended with a three-wicket haul with Brad Evans chipping in with two in total. Zimbabwe have an opportunty here as well if they are ambitiuos to go for the win. They have enough overs to make a game out of this one but will know that they can not lose wickets early. Will they be able to pull of a remarkable run chase? Or will West Indies set up this win with a stunning bowling performance? Let us not forget that rain could play spoilsport as well. We shall return shortly for the final innings of this Test match.

West Indies will hunt for a win here! They declare at 203 for the loss of five wickets and have set Zimbabwe a target of 272 runs to win. With the chances of rain around the horizon, they are in a comfortable position and should not lose the game from here. They came into Day 5 with all 10 wickets intact but lost their openers early with both Kraigg Brathwaite and Tagenarine Chanderpaul initially looking to preserve their wickets. Raymon Reifer and Jermaine Blackwood put on a 107-run partnership with the former playing the role of an anchor and Jermaine Blackwood looking to be slightly aggressive. They both perished after getting to their half-centuries and Roston Chase was dismissed early as well. However, they have enough runs on the board and will look to put some pressure on the hosts.
A couple of runs to end the over! Brad Evans bowls this short and on off, Kyle Mayers swats away towards wide of long on for two runs.
This is pitched up, on off, Kyle Mayers drives it towards covers.

FOUR! Good shot! Brad Evans lands this short and on middle, sticks to the surface a bit, Kyle Mayers goes for the pull shot, but is early into his shot. However, he still manages to generate enough power from the toe-end of his bat and gets a boundary at the deep mid-wicket fence.
The wind is picking up here and the dark clouds are collecting over the ground. There is some movement on the boundary line as well as the ground staff are out of their shed.
A slower one now, full and on middle, Joshua Da Silva works it off the inner half towards square leg for a run.
FOUR! Powered away! This is full and on middle, angling in, Joshua Da Silva gets his front leg out of the way and heaves it towards the vacant deep mid-wicket fence for a boundary.
Brad Evans loses his line and serves this full and down the leg side, Kyle Mayers goes after it and flicks it towards deep mid-wicket for a single.
FOUR! Paddles this one fine! Wellington Masakadza continues to bowl quick and strays down leg. Joshua Da Silva sweeps this towards fine leg for four more runs.
Floats this one full and into the stumps. Joshua Da Silva dabs this down to mid-wicket.
Bowls this short as well and spins into the pads. Kyle Mayers clips this towards deep square leg for a single.
Bowls this one short as well and outside off. Kyle Mayers punches this to deep cover-point and takes a couple of runs.
FOUR! Poor delivery and gets the treatment! Wellington Masakadza fires this one full and angles this down leg. Kyle Mayers sweeps and helps it along its way towards wide fine leg for four runs.
Wellington Masakadza bowls this short and outside off, Kyle Mayers rocks back and punches this towards cover.
Joshua Da Silva strides out to the middle.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! Brad Evans gets a breakthrough now! Zimbabwe with couple of quick blows to make things interesting here. Brad Evans serves this full and outside off, Roston Chase stays there and just throws his bat at it without any footwork. The ball takes the outside edge just after his bat hits the ground and goes towards the keeper where Tafadzwa Tsiga makes no mistake. Zimbabwe players are already celebrating but the two umpires have a chat and sends it upstairs to check and the soft singal is 'Not Out'. However, the replays confirms that there is an edge and the third umpire signals the red light. Roston Chase stays there in disbelief, but has to make that long walk back. West Indies lose half their side now.
Commentary.Howout: c Tafadzwa Tsiga b Brad Evans

Brad Evans continues bowling full here, on middle, Roston Chase clips it towards deep mid-wicket for one.

Commentary.Howout: c Tafadzwa Tsiga b Wellington Masakadza

Ends up lobbing it into the air over the bowler's head and Wellington Masakadza times his jump to perfection to hold onto the ball. Zimbabwe have got their third wicket but it is a little too late for them to hope for a win from here.

Attacks the stumps this time with the angle in from outside off on a good length. Raymon Reifer clips this to wide deep mid-wicket but they have to settle for a single.
Bowls this slightly fuller and outside the off stump. Raymon Reifer chooses to leave this one alone.
On a good length once again and just outside the off pole. Gets stuck in the wicket a bit and Jermaine Blackwood hits this uppishly towards long on for a run.

Bowls this one full and as well and outside the off pole. Raymon Reifer strokes this to the right of cover and takes a single.

That is FIFTY for Jermaine Blackwood and West Indies getting a move on now! Victor Nyauchi bowls this full and outside off. Jermaine Blackwood strokes this to wide long off and takes a single to reach his landmark.
Gives this one some air again, on middle, Raymon Reifer gets forward and turns it to the leg side.

Flighted, full and on off, Jermaine Blackwood prods forward and blocks it out.

A tad bit fuller this time and outside off. Jermaine Blackwood punches this straight towards long on and they take two runs comfortably.

Who will bowl from the other end? It will be Victor Nyauchi.

Slightly short and outside off. Jermaine Blackwood thumps this off his back foot towards long on for a run.
Flighted delivery once again and outside off. Raymon Reifer eases this down to long on for one.

We are back for the second session! The Zimbabwe are in a huddle just near the boundary ropes. Now they are spreading out and taking their respective field positions. Jermaine Blackwood and Raymon Reifer are already out in the middle to continue the West Indies innings. Wellington Masakadza to start proceedings with the ball in this session.
... DAY 5, SESSION 2 ...

West Indies were in trouble after losing both of their openers, who combined for more than half of the runs scored in their first innings. They needed someone to step up, and they found not one, but two batters who took the responsibility on themselves. Although, Jermaine Blackwood and Raymon Reifer struggled a bit initially, they remained patient and found their rhythm. Also, they picked their bowlers perfectly and showed intent to score runs at a brisk rate. They decided to attack Brandon Mavuta and did not let him settle down. Both of them have added 81 runs for the third wicket and will look to continue the momentum. It will be interesting to see if and when the Windies decide to declare their innings to have a go at the hosts and force a result. Join us for the second session at 4.10 pm IST (10.40 am GMT) to see how things pan out.

A session of two halves! West Indies currently lead by 199 runs, but they had to work hard to be in this position. Zimbabwe started well, getting rid of both the openers quite early on. They were in a good position to put more pressure on the middle order by picking up a few more wickets, but that was not the case, as they were not able to enjoy much success after that. They created a couple of chances here and there, but were not able to take it. Brad Evans was their best bowler this session, while Wellington Masakadza also supported him well. However, their best bowler from the first inning, Brandon Mavuta could not make any impact. They will need to come up with some different ideas in the second session to make a game out of this.

Drinks! Zimbabwe have been very disciplined and sticked to the basics and that is why they got the crucial wickets of both the West Indies openers. They know that they can test this middle order and put more pressure on them. Although West Indies currently lead by 121 runs, they require a partnership to get back on top. An excting phase of play awaits us.

We are all set for the final day to begin as the umpires are out in the middle. The Zimbabwe players are in a huddle before they disperse to their respective fielding positions. Kraigg Brathwaite and Tagenarine Chanderpaul will resume their opening partnership. Victor Nyauchi has been handed the ball and will begin proceedings in this morning session. Let's go...

Zimbabwe, on the other hand, would be high on confidence after their fightback on Day 4. Craig Ervine also took a brave decision to declare when they were trailing, but that also makes a huge statement about the team. Their main goal will be to use the conditions and get through the Windies' batting line-up as soon as possible. This Test match is in the balance at the moment, and if any of the teams suffers a major slip it could affect the result massively. Both teams will want to go for the win but at the back of their minds, they know they need to approach this carefully too. Stay tuned to catch all the updates about this game.

West Indies are currently leading by 89 runs with their openers still at the crease. However, if they are focusing on forcing a result they will need to treat this as an ODI match. They need to add runs quickly but also play sensibly so that there is no collapse. It will be tough to decide how many overs to bat as there are chances of rain too, but they need to give their bowlers a cushion to come in and try to get the result here.

Hello and a warm welcome folks! We are not far away from the start of the fifth and final Day of this right on the edge Test match between Zimbabwe and West Indies. Till now, we have seen everything, maiden Test fifties, centuries,  double-hundreds, rain-stoppages, record-breaking partnerships, surprising declarations, and much more. Although the most likely result is a draw, we have seen that in cricket anything is possible and that is why we can expect a thrilling day of Test cricket.
... DAY 5, SESSION 1 ...

Right then, a thrilling day of Test cricket comes to a close. The odds are heavily stacked towards this game ending as a draw but could we have a twist in the tale on the final day of this Test match? The forecast for the weather indicates that we may not have a full day of cricket but we expect it to still be exciting. Join us on Wednesday 8th July at 1 pm IST (7.30 am GMT) for all the action but our build-up as usual will begin in advance. Cheers!

Gary Ballance will have a few words to share as well. He admits that he was not aware of the fact that he is one of the three batters to make a hundred on debut for Zimbabwe. Mentions that it is a great start and he just wanted to contribute in order to get the team to a good position. Claims that there was a little bit of extra pressure but as he spent some time at the wicket, he felt confident and the ball was coming onto the bat better. Explains that it is a different challenge facing the different bowlers in the West Indies side as the pacers would bowl wicket to wicket and the ball would stay a bit low while there was spin on offer for the spinners as well.  Reckons that he did not have to give Brandon Mavuta any lessons as the shots he was playing were outstanding. Adds that he was timing the ball well and it is good to see him get to his fifty. Ends by saying the his preferred batting position is at number 5.

Brandon Mavuta is up for a chat. He says that he is over the moon and happy that his hard work is paying off. Adds that playing domestic cricket has helped him very much. Mentions that plan was to play the supporting role to Gary Ballance and to put away the loose balls. Tells that this was a big challenge for him to face the Windies bowlers and is satisfied with his performance.

The first session of Day 4 did not go as planned for Zimbabwe as they lost 4 wickets and looked in all sorts of trouble. Alzarri Joseph picked up a couple of wickets early including the set Innocent Kaia for 67 runs with Kemar Roach chipping in with one more. Gudakesh Motie broke a stubborn 45-run partnership between Gary Ballance and Wellington Masakadza as the latter played a rash shot just before Lunch. The middle session is when the recovery began for the hosts as they played through the whole period without losing a wicket. West Indies seemed to lack ideas and the turning point of the game arrived when Jason Holder dropped an absolute sitter to give Brandon Mavuta a life early in his inning. It will be interesting to see if West Indies will adopt an aggressive mentality on Day 5 and look for an unlikely win.

Zimbabwe went into the final session trailing by 134 runs with just three wickets in hand but they continued to chip away at the runs with the tail wagging. Gary Ballance held up one end and was unbeaten on 137 runs on his debut for the hosts when Craig Ervine decided to declare and have a go at the West Indies batters. Brandon Mavuta followed up his 5-wicket haul with a crucial half-century and added 135 runs with Gary before being dismissed by Jason Holder. Victor Nyauchi and Richard Ngarava played some hefty blows to bring the deficit down to 68. The West Indies openers managed to play out 13 overs without losing the wicket and will look to pick up the scoring in the final morning session of the Test match.

A day that well and truly belongs to Zimbabwe as they have fought hard to claw themselves out of a precarious position. Both teams will head into Day 5 knowing that they will need to play really badly to lose this game as a draw seems like the most likely result. The hosts entered Day 4 with their backs against the wall but have shown remarkable grit to bring this game on level footing. We have now had two full days of cricket but with the pitch playing well, there may not be enough time to get a result. West Indies have a lead of 89 runs and will still feel like they may be able to steal a win here if they start well on the last day.
